title: Occupational exposure to organic solvents during pregnancy and childhood behavior: findings from the PELAGIE birth cohort (France, 2002-2013).
ehr_evidence: The data source was the PELAGIE French birth cohort, with exposure and outcome data collected via parent-completed self-administered questionnaires (not EHR); 'Within the French birth cohort PELAGIE, parents assessed their children's internalizing and externalizing behaviors using items from the Child Behavior Checklist and the Preschool Social Behavior Questionnaire at age 2, and the Strength and Difficulties Questionnaire at age 6.'
summary: A prospective birth cohort study of 715 mother-child pairs in Brittany, France, examining whether maternal occupational exposure to organic solvents during pregnancy is associated with childhood externalizing and internalizing behavior traits at ages 2 and 6.
key_findings: Increased externalizing behavior score at age 2 was associated with prenatal solvent exposure (standardized coefficient 0.34, 95% CI 0.11-0.57 for occasional exposure and 0.26, 95% CI 0.05-0.48 for regular exposure) versus unexposed.
The association with externalizing behavior was attenuated and non-significant at age 6 (0.22, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.47 for occasional exposure and 0.07, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.28 for regular exposure).
No significant association was observed between prenatal solvent exposure and internalizing behavior at age 2 or age 6.
The association between prenatal solvent exposure and externalizing behavior at age 2 was stronger in girls (0.44, 95% CI 0.11-0.77) than in boys (0.23, 95% CI -0.09 to 0.55).
captured_features: Maternal occupational exposure to organic solvents (never/occasional/regular) self-reported early in pregnancy
Child behavior subscale scores from CBCL and PSBQ at age 2 and SDQ at age 6
Latent internalizing and externalizing behavior traits via structural equation modeling
Maternal age, maternal education, parity, child's sex, maternal tobacco consumption, breastfeeding duration, mother-child interaction score
pathologies_diseases: Externalizing behavior (aggression, opposition, attention deficit/hyperactivity, conduct problems, hyperactivity/inattention)
Internalizing behavior (emotional symptoms, peer relationship problems)
population: 715 mother-child pairs from the PELAGIE general-population cohort in Brittany, France; pregnant women enrolled before 19 weeks gestation (2002-2006); children assessed at ages 2 and 6.
limitations: Occupational exposure was based on maternal self-report and defined by frequency rather than intensity.
Behavior scores at age 2 were adapted from two scales (CBCL and PSBQ) not strictly validated.
Lack of measurement invariance between boys and girls prevented formal conclusions about sex-differential effects.
Other maternal/postnatal solvent exposure sources (home/outside) were largely unmeasured.
Analysis used a sub-sample of the cohort, though selection bias was likely minimal.
